deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f: X -> S, F a quasi-coherent O_X-module with a stratification relative to S. A stratification is a compatible family of isomorphisms p_1^*F ≅ p_2^*F on all infinitesimal neighbourhoods Δ_{X/S}(i) of the diagonal in X×_S X, satisfying the cocycle condition. In characteristic 0 for smooth X/S this is the same as an integrable connection.

Such an F defines a module on the stratifying site X_strat, the infinitesimal-type site whose objects are nilpotent thickenings of opens of X. Grothendieck makes its cohomology explicit through a cosimplicial sheaf C(F) on X_zar:
- C^n(F) = F^{(n)} = lim_i of the pullback of F to Δ^n_{X/S}(i).
- Here Δ^n_{X/S}(i) is the i-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal X -> X^{n+1}_S (fibre product over S).
- The pullback may be taken along any of the n+1 projections. The stratification identifies these pullbacks canonically, so C^n(F) is well defined.
- Since Δ^n(i) has the same underlying space as X, C^n(F) is a sheaf on X_zar. It is the completed tensor product of the formal neighbourhood algebra of the diagonal with F.
- The coface maps of C(F) are only f^{-1}O_S-linear (differential operators), not O_X-linear.

The boxed comparison is H^*(X_strat, F) ≅ H^*(X_zar, C^*(F)), where the right side is the hypercohomology of the associated complex. This is a Čech–Alexander computation of infinitesimal/stratifying cohomology. In the smooth char-0 case it reduces, via the formal Poincaré lemma, to de Rham cohomology of the connection.

Grothendieck then contrasts two cohomology theories:
- (a) Zariski cohomology H^i(X_zar, F) of any quasi-coherent F;
- (b) stratifying cohomology H^i(X_strat, F) of a stratified F, computed by the formula above.
A struck-out sentence says neither seems, at first sight, to contain the other.

The next page resolves the asymmetry by linearization. Any quasi-coherent F gives a stratified pro-quasi-coherent module Q°(F) = lim_n P^n_{X/S} ⊗ F whose stratifying cohomology is the Zariski cohomology of F. Q° is functorial for differential operators. If the diagonal is a nilpotent immersion, Q°(F) = f^*f_*F. Hence the Zariski hypercohomology of a complex of differential operators is the stratifying cohomology of a complex of stratified modules.

Purpose: preparing the comparison 'de Rham cohomology = infinitesimal/crystalline cohomology' for the December 1966 IHES lectures. This material became 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968).
errors: No mathematical error, but the hypercohomology identification needs care. C^n(F) is a projective limit, so one needs Mittag-Leffler / lim^1-vanishing arguments; these hold for quasi-coherent F on affines because the transition maps are surjective. Grothendieck does not state this here.
Calling C(F) a cosimplicial sheaf 'sur X_zar' is fine only as a sheaf of f^{-1}O_S-modules. Grothendieck flags this himself on the next page ('différentielles ne sont pas linéaires').

deep.surprise_reason: These are preparatory lecture notes for the December 1966 IHES 'laïus' on crystals. Everything here (stratifying site, Čech–Alexander computation, and on the next page linearization of differential operators) appears in Grothendieck's 1968 Crystals exposé and was systematized by Berthelot. The only mildly interesting points are historical: the dating and the struck-out remark that neither cohomology theory seems to contain the other.
transcription_corrections: The left margin of the target space reads 'X_strat' in the first occurrence and 'X_str' (abbreviated) inside the boxed formula.

The struck-out passage under 'deux théories cohomologiques' seems to read roughly 'aucune ne semble, à première vue, plus générale que l'autre / ne pas contenir l'autre'. It is heavily crossed out; the machine reading 'distinctes' is doubtful.
'C^n(F) = F^{(n)}' is correct; Δ^n_{X/S}(i) carries index n as superscript and (i) as the order of the infinitesimal neighbourhood.
